title: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Australia Minimum Wage 2026 and State Differences
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the australia minimum wage 2026. Includes state differences in ordinary-time earnings, tax, and super.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, giving an annual gross of about $52,253 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, an hourly rate of $30 gives an annual gross of $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What are the state differences in ordinary-time earnings?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary-time earnings vary across states and territories. While the national average is $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), states such as New South Wales and Victoria often exceed this, while others like Tasmania and South Australia may be below. These differences reflect industry mix, cost of living, and local labour markets. For a precise comparison, refer to the ABS average weekly earnings data for your state.

faqs.q: How does the australia minimum wage 2026 affect my pay?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award rates may be higher than the minimum, and superannuation (12%) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. Always check your award or enterprise agreement, as the minimum wage is a floor, not a target.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

Knowing how to turn your hourly rate into an annual salary is essential whether you are negotiating a job offer, budgeting, or comparing pay across roles. The standard formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, as this is the ordinary hours defined under the Fair Work Act. For example, if you earn $35 per hour, your annual gross pay would be $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160.

This calculation gives you a gross annual figure before tax and superannuation. It assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also does not account for salary sacrifice or other deductions. For a more tailored estimate, you can use [the timesheet](/) on our site, where you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

### The Role of the Fortnight

Many Australian employers pay wages fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the $35 per hour example, your weekly pay is $35 × 38 = $1,330, so your fortnightly gross is $2,660. This can help you align your budget with your pay cycle.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Australia’s labour market is not uniform. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data that shows significant variation across states and territories. As of May 2026, the national average for full-time adult ordinary-time earnings is $2,083.70 per week. However, this is an average across all states and does not represent any single job’s median.

Workers in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory typically earn above the national average, driven by concentrations of high-paying industries such as finance, professional services, and public administration. In contrast, Tasmania and South Australia often report lower averages due to a higher share of industries like hospitality and retail. Western Australia’s earnings can fluctuate with the mining sector.

These state differences matter when you are converting an hourly rate to annual pay. A rate that is competitive in one state may be below average in another. For a broader view of pay levels, see our [reference tables](/data) which include national and state averages from the ABS.

## Tax and Superannuation on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate tax and super. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) sets the resident tax rates for 2026–27 as follows:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold is included in the rates above. For a single person earning $69,160, the tax would be roughly $11,367 plus Medicare, but this is an estimate only. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more detail.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For the $35 per hour example, your employer would contribute an additional $8,299 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## The Australia Minimum Wage 2026

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. This is the legal floor; many awards and enterprise agreements provide higher rates.

If you are paid at or near the minimum, your annual gross would be $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,253. After tax and Medicare, your take-home pay would be around $41,000, depending on your circumstances. Remember that super is on top, so your total employment cost to the employer is about $58,523.

For award-covered employees, check your specific award rate, which may be higher than the national minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each industry. Our [pay guides](/blog) page can help you find the right award.

## Putting It All Together

Converting hourly to annual pay is a simple calculation, but context matters. State differences in ordinary-time earnings mean that the same hourly rate can represent very different living standards depending on where you live. Always consider the full picture: gross pay, tax, super, and any loadings or penalties.

Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see how your rate stacks up against the australia minimum wage 2026 and national averages. And remember, the figures here are estimates. For a binding determination of your pay, consult your employer, award, or a workplace relations professional.
